name: vacuum-filtration-cake-build
title: Vacuum Filtration Cake Build
description: A card-scale processing/progress indicator modelled on Büchner-funnel vacuum filtration: liquid drips through a filter paper as a solids cake builds on its surface, the drip cadence visibly stretching from 0.6s to 2.4s per drop as the thickening cake adds resistance, per Darcy's law.
useWhen: a processing/upload/sync indicator wants an honest 'work is slowing down as it accumulates cost' identity instead of a generic determinate progress bar or spinner — the mechanism is a real Darcy-law filtration decay (drip interval inversely tied to a growing cake's resistance), so the slowdown itself is the signal, not a fake stall. Pick barograph-drum-week instead when the point is a long-running, unattended recording trace with no completion event at all, or gauge-capacity-waterline when the point is a level against a hard legal/contractual limit rather than a rate that decays toward a cyclical reset.
instruction: A card-scale single-canvas component modelling Büchner-funnel vacuum filtration: liquid drips through filter paper into a receiving flask while a solids cake builds on the paper's surface, and under constant applied pressure the filtration rate decays as the cake thickens (Darcy's law: flow rate is inversely proportional to total resistance, which grows with cake height). All geometry derives from the chart wrapper's getBoundingClientRect via computeGeo(W, H): a funnel (wide top rim tapering to a paper line at paperY, paper radius = minDim * 0.22), a narrow stem dripping down to a visible tip, and a flask (neck, tapered shoulder, flat-bottomed body) built as a single closed polygon path (flaskPath) reused for both its stroke and, via ctx.clip(), the liquid fill region — so the liquid is always exact against the tapered silhouette with no separate area math. Cake height follows the constant-pressure Darcy relation h(t) = sqrt(2*K*t) (K tuned so h(14) = HMAX = 0.38 of the paper radius) over a 14s fill phase; drip interval is sampled continuously as interval(t) = 0.6s * (H0 + h(t)) / H0 where H0 = HMAX/3 stands in for the paper's own baseline resistance (so the formula never divides by zero at t=0) — this produces the spec's exact 0.6s-to-2.4s, 4x slowdown, not a fixed schedule. Drops are spawned on a deterministic schedule (stepSim walks nextDropAtMs forward by dripInterval(t) each spawn) and each animates a real ~260ms gravity-eased (p^2) departure-from-stem-to-splash arc — always far shorter than the shortest 0.6s interval, so the slowing cadence reads from the GAP between arcs, never from the arc itself; on landing, the flask's liquidLevelPx rises by dropStepPx = 5px scaled by (minDim / 260) (the spec's reference px number at reference card size), and a brief 180ms fading ripple marks the splash point. At the 14s mark the cake and drip cadence freeze at their final state, a 6-particle bubble-burst animates for 400ms at the cake surface (vacuum release), then a shared contentAlpha ramps 1 to 0 over 1500ms fading ONLY the cake, liquid and burst — the funnel/flask glass silhouette, drawn every frame from --border at a fixed 0.7 alpha (0.85 for the load-bearing paper line), never fades, since it is fixed apparatus, not process state. Full loop is 14000 + 400 + 1500 = 15900ms, after which the simulation resets to empty and restarts — unbounded. The cake itself is a filled top-half ellipse (ctx.ellipse from angle PI to 2*PI, a true semicircular profile when height equals radius) with a radial gradient from --foreground at its apex to --ns-muted at its rim, densest at center; the liquid is --foreground at 55% alpha filled through the flask clip. Colour is read once via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue for --foreground, --border and --ns-muted with no literal fallback of any kind; if any is empty (stylesheet not yet applied) the mount loop retries on the next rAF and paints nothing until all three resolve. A MutationObserver on document.documentElement's class attribute re-reads tokens on every theme flip and forces a resize + (if reduced motion) a redraw of the static frame; a ResizeObserver on the chart wrapper recomputes geometry and resizes the canvas backing store (capped devicePixelRatio 2); an IntersectionObserver stops driving new frames while off-screen and, on re-entering view, re-reads tokens and restarts the simulation from empty (never resumes a stale mid-cycle state) — no paint happens on any of these three paths before a token read succeeds. Under prefers-reduced-motion the component runs zero rAF loops and zero timers: it deterministically simulates (same stepSim function, called in a tight synchronous walk rather than per-frame) the fill phase up to t = 14 * 0.6 = 8.4s (60% through the cycle — cake at h(8.4)/HMAX ≈ 77% of its max, i.e. ~29% of the paper radius, several drops already landed and the flask level risen), then pins exactly one drop mid-fall (started 130ms before the freeze instant) so the frozen frame shows a departure-to-splash arc in flight alongside the built-up cake and risen flask level, not just static endpoints — the same frame on every load. Cleanup on unmount cancels both the animation and token-wait rAF handles and disconnects all three observers. Zero dependencies, DOM+canvas only, no color literal anywhere including fallbacks.
